title: Embedded Payments Go-to-Market Strategy: How to Drive Adoption
summary: Build an embedded payments go-to-market strategy for SaaS. Improve merchant onboarding, market the workflow and measure payments attach rate and active usage.
body_markdown:
Table of Contents


Toggle


Launching an embedded payments integration is only part of the process. The hard part is getting your customer to enable payments within your application. SaaS providers can successfully integrate payments but still struggle to get their merchants to activate them within the app. If only a small percentage of your merchants activate embedded payments, you may not see the additional revenue you anticipated. Getting adoption requires commercial ownership as well as technical integration. This guide focuses on the go-to-market strategy (GTM), marketing messaging and sales motions required to transform payments from a feature into a revenue stream.


Here, merchants are the businesses using your SaaS product to collect payments from their own customers.


### Key Takeaways


- An embedded payments go-to-market strategy needs ownership across product, sales, onboarding and support.
- Measure payments attach rate with a clear denominator and activity period, then track active usage and transaction volume.
- Lead with merchant workflows, transparent pricing and practical switching support.
- Use separate adoption motions for new merchants and existing customers. Approval alone is not a first payment.


##


Why Embedded Payments Matter to Your SaaS Business


[Embedded payments](https://www.cashfree.com/embedded-payments/) aren’t merely a feature you can check off the list; they can also enhance your competitive advantage by improving merchant workflows and retention, and provide additional revenue opportunities through transactions your merchants choose to process on your platform.


Embedded payments will also offer benefits to your merchants. The first is reduced complexity since your merchants will not have to integrate separately with each financial institution or payment processor. Second, embedded payments enable your merchants to manage collections in the same location where they currently manage their businesses. Funds settle to the merchant’s designated bank account under the agreed payment arrangement.


In fact,[EY-Parthenon’s research](https://www.ey.com/en_us/insights/payments/embedded-payments-shift-from-utility-to-growth-engine) indicated that among platforms that saw payments as a means of driving platform growth, 30% cited customer experience and improved retention as key objectives for embedded payments. This should be a major consideration as you develop your sales strategy.


##


The SaaS Payments Adoption Gap


Launching embedded payments and achieving successful merchant adoption are different milestones.


EY-Parthenon and Finix surveyed platforms and merchants in June 2024 and discovered that approximately 40% of non-financial services platforms surveyed had never integrated payments. Of those that did embed payments, only 58% achieved greater than 50% utilization of their payments solutions. Additionally, 70% viewed payments as a utility rather than a potential source of growth.


Why is this? The answer is simple. Merchants already have a method to accept money. Making the merchant switch to your method requires making the switch easy, worthwhile, and obvious to the merchant.

##


What Is Payments Attach Rate?


In this guide, payments attach rate is defined as the number of merchants on your platform using your payments product divided by the total number of merchants on your platform, multiplied by 100. Define “using” with a consistent activity window, such as at least one successful live payment in the past 30 days.


For example, if you have 1,000 merchants on your platform and 300 of them use your payments product, your payments attach rate would be 30%.


Attach rate measures breadth.


Wallet share measures how much of a single merchant’s overall payment activity flows through your platform. Both are important metrics. Achieving a high attach rate while having very little average merchant payment volume can generate less revenue than achieving a lower attach rate with merchants that send most of their payment activity through your platform.


Do not count an application or approval as active payment usage. If some platform merchants are ineligible for your payment product, also report an eligible-merchant attach rate and label the denominator. Benchmark reports may use different definitions for attachment, adoption and active use.


##


Give Your Embedded Payments Go-to-Market Strategy an Owner


Ownership of embedded payments means there has to be one named person. A clear single owner for all things payments, from product to sales, onboarding, support, finance, and risk, ensures there is accountability for adoption. According to the 2026 benchmark study, companies with a C-suite level payments lead had a median take rate 45 basis points greater than their peers who did not have a dedicated payments lead. This is an association in that survey; appointing a leader does not guarantee that uplift.


Identify the funnel stages. Track each stage separately, with payment volume measured alongside merchant conversion:


- Invitation
- Application
- Approval
- First payment
- Retained usage


This will give you insight into where merchants are falling off the funnel.


Determine which segment to start with. New customers and existing customers will need different approaches. Choose one.


Work in three month cycles (30 days, 60 days and 90 days). Establish a baseline and pick out one bottleneck to fix within the first 30 days. Test the solution in the next 30 days. Deploy what works during the last 30 days.


### Turn Funnel Drop-Offs into a 90-Day Adoption Plan


**Funnel signal** **Question to investigate** **Useful next action**


Invited but not applying Is the workflow benefit clear, and is the merchant eligible? Test a relevant in-product message with a defined merchant segment


Applied but not approved Are documents, business details or verification steps incomplete? Show the pending requirement and assign an onboarding owner


Approved but no first payment Is checkout configured, and does the merchant know how to use it? Help the merchant complete a legitimate first customer payment


First payment but no retained usage Is the product solving an ongoing workflow problem? Review the experience, support issues and share of payment volume


For each stage, compare conversion and elapsed time for the same merchant cohort. Measure payment volume alongside the funnel rather than treating it as another application status.

##


Marketing Embedded Payments: Lead with the Merchant Workflow


Merchants want to get paid reliably, chase fewer invoices and spend less time matching money to orders. Faster settlement can also matter, but the message should reflect the merchant’s actual problem and the payment terms you can offer.


This should shape how you approach marketing embedded payments.


Promote the workflow, not the feature. Show how embedded payments fit inside of a process that merchants already run, such as collecting deposits or sending[payment requests](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/) after a job is done.


Show them the cost clearly. Help merchants compare what they pay today for their current solutions vs. what they would pay on your platform. Only use fees and numbers that you can verify.


Use in-app prompts at the right moment in the workflow (such as when creating an invoice) instead of sending out a single email.


Run ongoing campaigns and assign someone to own the number of adopted users.


##


Price Embedded Payments for Value and Sustainable Adoption


Merchants may see price as an issue; however, lower prices alone will not resolve concerns about onboarding, reliability, settlement or switching effort. Compare the full cost and workflow value while keeping your own economics sustainable.


You also need to think about packaging your product or service. Under your agreed partner pricing structure, you may add a profit margin above your payment processing costs. Confirm the supported charging and commission model rather than assuming a monthly billing method. No matter how you set up your pricing structure, be certain that your client knows what they are paying and why. A merchant that does not know how much they will pay for something is unlikely to start using it.


##


Drive SaaS Payments Adoption During Onboarding


Onboarding can be an effective moment to introduce payments because the merchant is already setting up their workflow. This makes it a useful place to focus SaaS payments adoption, while keeping the activation choice and terms clear.


Include payment processing with sign-up. Prompt merchants to enable payment processing during the initial sign-up process instead of months down the road.


Remove approval blockers early. Ask for[merchant onboarding and KYC information](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/merchant-onboarding-process/) early in the process, inform merchants whether or not they qualify for the product/service and provide an estimate of how long the approval process will take. Final activation remains subject to verification and approval.


Track time to first payment. Verify that all configurations and training were completed prior to transferring ownership of the merchant to your support staff.


##


Selling Payments to Existing Customers


Selling payment processing products to current clients can be more difficult. They currently have a provider and a workflow that is working well.


Start with discovery. Find out where merchants enter their data, how they correlate payments to invoices, and which payment options their clients want. The problems that merchants experience can give clues into what you should market to them.


Target accounts which are approved but inactive. Merchants sometimes receive approvals and fail to make a single payment. Contact these merchants, determine the problem that prevented them from activating payment services, and assist them through the activation process.


Use account reviews to bring up payment services. Customer success teams can bring up payment services during regularly scheduled reviews with clients.


Do not hide switching costs. Provide merchants with a detailed transition plan that explains the effort, dependencies and responsibilities involved in switching to your payment services.


##


How to Handle Common Embedded Payments Objections


You can anticipate some resistance (especially from current customers) once you begin asking merchants to utilize embedded payments. The following are common objections raised by merchants and ways to address them:


### “We already have a provider.”


Show them the difference it will make in terms of the number of tools they must deal with, and the time spent manually reconciling different systems. In many cases, fewer tools and less reconciliation time will be a more compelling case than simply lower fees.


### “Our saved cards and payment history are with another provider.”


Be transparent regarding what information will transfer over and what won’t, and provide merchants with a clear plan for transitioning. Confirm whether[stored-card tokens](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/types-of-tokenization-integration/) can be migrated through the providers’ supported process. Card details, tokens and historical transaction records require separate treatment.


### “How will refunds, disputes and chargebacks be handled?”


Explain clearly how refunds,[disputes](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-disputes/) and[chargebacks](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/chargebacks-meaning-how-they-works-types-causes-prevention/) will be processed within your platform before merchants commit to switching. Name the support owner, response timelines and evidence the merchant may need to provide.


### “Will this affect our accounting system?”


Demonstrate how payment information will flow into existing reporting and integrated systems used by your merchants. Map the fields available in your[embedded payments reports](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/partners/embedded/reports/reports) to the merchant’s accounting workflow.


##


Keep Sales, Onboarding and Support Messaging Consistent


Sales, onboarding & support teams will hear the same questions over and over again. Provide them with shared resources that answer commonly asked questions in the same way.


- Provide a short explanation of what payment processing does for the merchant
- Give them guidance through the application and KYC process
- Present them with answers to frequently asked objections
- Develop a troubleshooting pathway for setup problems, using[Dev Studio](https://www.cashfree.com/devstudio) to demonstrate checkout flows where useful
- Define clear rules for when to escalate issues


The more consistent the story from each team member, the greater trust merchants will have in it.


##


Measure Payments Attach Rate Alongside Active Usage and Revenue


Evaluate the success of your payments attach rate on a regular basis (monthly), and evaluate it against each funnel stage.


If you see high invitation rates but low application rates, then your message may not be landing, or eligibility and perceived effort may be blocking applications.


If you see approval rates are high but first payment rates are low, then there may be an issue during setup or activation. Investigate the reasons at the stage with the largest material drop-off before choosing a fix.


You should also use total contribution as a measurement method for how successful your payments program is. A higher fee charged on lower active volume can produce lower total revenue. Distinguish payment volume, gross fees and the commission retained by your platform, then account for incentives and the support costs you bear.

##


Conclusion


Embedded payments only work when used by merchants. Treat payment as a product launch that never ends, give it an owner, measure each stage of the funnel, lead with the workflow and make activation part of onboarding. Doing so makes your payment attach rate a growth lever, not a disappointment.

FAQs


#### How do you sell embedded payments to SaaS customers?


Use the workflow that the merchant has always run through, provide a clear cost comparison, prompt for activation at onboarding time, follow up with all the merchants that were approved but never made a payment.


#### What is an attach rate for payments?


An attach rate for payments represents the percentage of merchants utilizing your platform that also utilize your embedded payment solution. If 300 of your 1,000 merchants utilize your embedded payment solution, then your attach rate would be 30%.


#### What is a good payments attach rate?


Good is defined by your vertical, maturity, merchant eligibility and metric definition. The Q1 2026 survey cited above reported that 78% of vertical SaaS platforms targeted a payments adoption rate of 71% or higher, while only 25% had reached it. That adoption benchmark should not be treated as a universal attach-rate target.


#### How do you get existing customers to switch to embedded payments?


Do discovery to find what pains exist for your customer, raise payments during account reviews, provide a transition plan that helps them manage migration risks.


#### Who should own embedded payments inside a SaaS company?


One accountable person with authority to coordinate product, sales, support, finance and risk. Each team still needs a clear role in onboarding, activation and ongoing merchant usage.
